Definition: from G2351; to be in tumult, i.e. disturb, clamor:--make ado (a noise), trouble self, set on an uproar.
BiblicalUsage: The word thorybéō carries the sense of to make a tumult, to disturb. In Matthew 9:23, Jesus came into the ruler's house, and it appears again in Mark 5:39.
TheologicalSignificance: Flute players and a noisy crowd at a dead girl's house show me how quickly people mistake noise for grief and bustle for help.
